significance: A hill temple complex to Murugan at Chettikulam in Perambalur district, ascribed to a Pandya king named Kulasekhara and reached by 240 steps. Its four-foot swayambhu image is unusual in showing the god with hair and holding a sugarcane marked with eleven divisions, and on the third to fifth days of the Tamil month of Masi the setting sun's rays climb the deity from foot to face.
story: Murugan is said to have been given the sugarcane by his mother Parvati in congratulation for defeating the demons, and to have carried it to this hill.
